Flex-start

\r\n

\r\n To shift your elements over to the left, simply add the class names \r\n \"flex-group\" and \"flex-start\" to your parent wrapper.\r\n

\r\n
\r\n flex-group flex-start\r\n

Flex-column

\r\n

\r\n If you want to display your elements vertically and still be mobile friendy, please add \r\n \"flex-group\" and \"flex-column\" to your parent wrapper.\r\n

\r\n
\r\n flex-group flex-column\r\n

Flex-stretch

\r\n

\r\n Not so commonly used, but if you want to maintain the same height of your elements, you can use \r\n \"flex-group\" and \"flex-stretch\" to your parent wrapper.\r\n

\r\n
\r\n flex-group flex-stretch\r\n

Space-between

\r\n

\r\n Distance your elements across the x-axis with \"flex-group\" and \"space-between\" on your parent wrapper. You \r\n can also group child sets and space these out as illustrated below in the second example.\r\n

\r\n
\r\n flex-group space-between\r\n

Flex-center & flex-align-center

\r\n

\r\n You may want to display your child elements centrally across the x-axis, in which case add \r\n \"flex-group\" and \"flex-center\" to your parent wrapper. \r\n

\r\n

\r\n Note: Although the above flex-center method will center both the x and y axis, for most cases you will only \r\n want to center the y-axis. In these situations, add \"flex-group\" and \"flex-align-center\" to your parent wrapper.\r\n

\r\n
\r\n flex-group flex-center\r\n

Prevent wrapping on a string (uses truncation)

\r\n
\r\n flex-group\r\n
flex-5, ellipsis This uses the same principle as seen at the top \r\n of this page under the heading \"Flex-group\" For this to work we need to truncate the text by including the class \".ellipsis\". Please remember to add a \r\n title tag to display the full string/value. \r\n
