Header

\r\n
\r\n

All Apps will now be using the same markup as the header displayed here in \r\n Design Language. To see the actual markup for this, please view the gist \r\n file on the right side of this page.

\r\n
\r\n
\r\n

Modifying the App logo

\r\n \r\n

We've made the App logo much easier to update. We now use the \r\n Material Icons \r\n for the specific App branding. Just pass in your chosen icon friendy name.

\r\n \r\n

Updating your App logo colours

\r\n

You will then need to decide on the background, foreground and border colours for your chosen App branding. \r\n The list of available colour classnames can be seen in the Attributes table on the right.\r\n

\r\n

Header secondary

\r\n
\r\n

There is an option available to include a secondary header. The secondary header is fixed, similar to the main page \r\n header. This allows the page content to scroll beneath. For this to work correctly in your App there a two things you'll \r\n need to do. Firstly, in your app.components.ts file add a HostBinding @HostBinding('attr.id') secondaryHeader = 'show-header-secondary';. \r\n Secondly, add the actual html element for the header inside app.component.html with the \r\n class name header-secondary. This will pick up the correct css from Design Language and reposition the core anglo-framework \r\n left navigation, main content container and any blades used.\r\n

\r\n
